Preview the inquiry guide

The licensed guide offers same-screen procedural questions, relevant Word drafts, deadline review and exception follow-ups. Accounts and plan access are stored; case information is not.

  1. Complaint receipt: For an oral complaint, provide reasonable assistance to put it in writing. Once a written complaint is received, use acknowledgement, registration, reference allocation and preliminary scrutiny drafts as appropriate.
  2. Competence and safeguards: Verify the competent IC/LC, applicable procedure, limitation, constitution and conflicts. An unresolved issue needs an owned follow-up and lawful next action.
  3. Voluntary conciliation: Explain the option. A Section 10 request is the aggrieved woman’s choice before inquiry; a monetary settlement cannot be its basis. Record the actual request, response and settlement steps, if any.
  4. Inquiry: Track actual notices, document receipt, responses, hearings, attendance, evidence and witnesses. Verified commencement is separate from the first meeting.
  5. Report and follow-through: Review the 90-day inquiry period, report within 10 days of completion and implementation within 60 days of receipt of recommendations, using the applicable statutory triggers.

Principal completion routes are lawful conciliation and inquiry/report. Referral or another procedural exception requires a reasoned next action; the tool does not turn it into a completed statutory inquiry.
